title: What is known about 1RB1RD_0RC0RD_0LD1LE_1LC0RB_1LF---_1LA0LE
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RD_0RC0RD_0LD1LE_1LC0RB_1LF---_1LA0LE.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: Open. The tape is just two blocks, (10)x then 0y, but x moves irregularly from one visit of the right end to the next (no affine rule fits); the width is only 2,593 after 109 steps.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (E1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 2,604 cells have been visited and 1,710 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: No halt in the first 1.18·10<sup>11</sup> steps (accelerated run)
claims.text: The run-length simulator tools/py/bbtools/rleaccel.py (blocks of 2 cells, runs crossed in one step, and cycle jumps, each used only after its one-cycle rule has been proved symbolically for all lengths; tested cell for cell against direct runs) runs 196,000,000 macro steps from blank tape without a halt. That is more than 1.18·1011 machine steps; the tape then spans 12,998 cells.

claims.title: Growth shape: power/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.314). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.367).

claims.title: The structure of the run
claims.text: Bouncer whose tape is (10)^x 0^y: a block of 10 pairs and a block of 0s, the width growing by 4 per event; x jumps irregularly between events, often by one when y is about 2x.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. No closed rule set has been found; see the README for what a proof would need.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. This page runs the machine in your browser and describes the structure seen in its run.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 2,604 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
two-block bouncer with an irregular exchange (chaotic)

sections.heading: What the tape looks like
html: At the moments the head is at the right end in state B, the tape is (10)x 0y (sometimes with a short marker 10 000 or a final 1), and the width 2x + y grows by 4 per event. Between events x moves irregularly: up by one when y is close to 2x, otherwise by jumps of either sign. The visited tape grows very slowly (2,593 cells after 109 steps).

sections.heading: Where it could halt
html: The only halting transition is E reading 1. A closed tape language with windows of 6 cells (bbtools.ctl) covers the run but still allows halts, with only a local constraint near the head: the head cell and the cells to its right read one of 101010, 101011, 101110, 111010, 111011. Nothing confines a halt to an edge.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.314). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.367).
After 109 steps the tape spans 2,604 cells (1,230 left of the start, 927 right), with a density of 1s of 0.657.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: Bouncer whose tape is (10)^x 0^y: a block of 10 pairs and a block of 0s, the width growing by 4 per event; x jumps irregularly between events, often by one when y is about 2x.
family: two-block bouncer with an irregular exchange (chaotic)
